metadata.note: The Western and Atlantic Railroad of the State of Georgia, Atlanta - Chattanooga (137 mi), built and still owned by the State, drawn as one feature per drawable span and operator (Rule 4): the State of Georgia's staged openings 1845-1851 to the [OPEN] 1862 end, the State again 1867[OPEN]-1870, the Western & Atlantic Railroad Company (lessee) 1871-1890, the Nashville, Chattanooga and St. Louis (lessee) 1891-1957 and the Louisville and Nashville 1957-1971, plus the NC&StL's Kingston - Rome branch 1897-1943. Same track, different operators: the State-era and lessee-company features share the historic-alignment geometry; the NC&StL and L&N features share the modern-track geometry.
metadata.ownership_split: State of Georgia (company 'Western and Atlantic Railroad (State of Georgia)') 1845-1862 in four staged pieces (each draws only its own piece, so no year draws unopened track) and 1867-1870 whole line; Western and Atlantic Railroad Company (private lessee, Joseph E. Brown) 1871-1890; Nashville, Chattanooga and St. Louis Railway 1891-1957; Louisville and Nashville Railroad 1957-1971 (shared boundary year 1957, as nashville_lines.geojson does). NOT splits: the L&N's 1880 purchase of 55% of NC&StL stock; the 1886 gauge change. The State and the lessee company are different real-world companies and carry different company strings and colours.
metadata.colours: NC&StL #BC6C25 and L&N #7A4419 pulled programmatically from data/nashville_lines.geojson. The two W&A companies are new to data/: State of Georgia #611C72, Western and Atlantic Railroad Company #299DA5, both checked unused by any company in data/.
metadata.omitted: Not drawn, per the report's drawable fields: United States Military Railroads 1863/64 - 25 Sep 1865 (a military supply road; no civilian passenger train in hand - drawable NONE), leaving a deliberate gap 1863-1866; the Rome Railroad as its own company 1849-1896 (separate company, needs its own report); the L&N's Knoxville - Atlanta trains over the W&A from Cartersville (Junta) and the earlier M&NG/AK&N trains from Marietta (trackage-rights trains of another road - belong in an L&N feature); excursions and specials (1962 General centennial run, post-1971 charters - none sourced, not passenger service established). The last ~1.1 mi into Chattanooga Union Station (tracks lifted) is not drawn.
metadata.freight_only_check: Every feature ends with passenger service: the main line's last train ran 30 Apr 1971 (CSX's W&A Subdivision is freight-only today and is not drawn after 1971); the Rome Branch ends with its 1943 abandonment; the CSX Tyner Branch (industrial) and the Kingston wye (staging) are not drawn.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: [OPEN] ends: all four State-era pieces (wa-state-atlanta-marietta, wa-state-marietta-calhoun, wa-state-calhoun-dalton, wa-state-dalton-chattanooga) end at 1862, the last confirmed year, not a known end (1863 W&A timetable at railga not read; true end Sep 1863 - Sep 1864 by stretch). [OPEN] start: wa-state-atlanta-chattanooga-postwar starts at 1867, the first confirmed post-war year (1865-66 unconfirmed). Dalton - Chattanooga opening May 1850 vs May 1851 (drawn 1851). Marietta - Calhoun intermediate openings (Kingston 1844/1845 vs ICC 1846). Rome Branch: no 1897-1942 timetable read; NC&StL acquisition c.1894 / 1896 / deed Dec 1896. Whether USMRR ran civilian passenger trains 1864-65 (Duke 1864 USMRR timetable broadside, unread). Last-train date 30 Apr vs 1-2 May 1971; Dixie Flyer end 12 vs 20 Jan 1966; Georgian name dropped 1968? Undated NC&StL relocations Kennesaw - Marietta and Rocky Face/Dalton. All headways and speeds except the 1867 and 1951 data points are estimates.

segments.note: The first operating leg of Georgia's state-owned railroad, Atlanta (then Marthasville; Union Depot from 1853) - Bolton - Vinings - Smyrna - Marietta. Start: railga.com/watl.html - 'Regular service on the W&A did not begin until 1845' (the Dec 23 1842 Marthasville - Marietta run was an inaugural trip with a locomotive hauled from Madison by wagon, trimmed); schafluetzel.org - 'the first 22 miles from Marietta to Atlanta were completed in September 1845'; ICC valuation - Atlanta - Marietta 'prior to 1845'. The Georgia Railroad reached Atlanta in Sep 1845, giving the W&A its first connection. This 1862 end is [OPEN]: it is the last CONFIRMED passenger year (the State's scheduled passenger train hauled by the General when it was seized at Big Shanty on 12 Apr 1862, the Andrews Raid), NOT a known end. Trains almost certainly ran in 1863 (railga lists an 1863 W&A timetable, not read) and until the Union armies took each stretch in Sep 1863 (Chattanooga) to May-Sep 1864 (the rest). Do not extend without evidence. headway_min 720 (about two trains a day each way) is an ESTIMATE, not sourced for this year range.
sources: Segment-level: start from railga.com, schafluetzel.org and the ICC valuation abstract; the [OPEN] 1862 end from the Great Locomotive Chase (Wikipedia, Western and Atlantic Railroad).

segments.note: Dalton - Rocky Face - Tunnel Hill (Chetoogeta tunnel) - Ringgold - Graysville - Chickamauga TN - Boyce - Chattanooga, completing through Atlanta - Chattanooga service (Nashville & Chattanooga connection from 1854). START CONFLICT, recorded: Wikipedia's W&A milepost table - tunnel completed 7 May 1850 and 'the first through passenger train passed that day'; schafluetzel.org - tunnel opened 9 May 1850; ICC - track Dalton - Chattanooga completed 'prior to December 1849'; Phillips (1908) p.318 - 'The last rails were laid in the spring of 1851. In May of that year the first train ran to Chattanooga.' Drawn from 1851, the later end of the conflict, per the governing principle; 1850 is very probably right and should be adopted if Johnston's 1931 W&A history or a May 1850 newspaper confirms the first through train. The Andrews Raid of 12 Apr 1862 ran north over this section (the chase ended just north of Ringgold), confirming 1862 here too. This 1862 end is [OPEN]: it is the last CONFIRMED passenger year (the State's scheduled passenger train hauled by the General when it was seized at Big Shanty on 12 Apr 1862, the Andrews Raid), NOT a known end. Trains almost certainly ran in 1863 (railga lists an 1863 W&A timetable, not read) and until the Union armies took each stretch in Sep 1863 (Chattanooga; Ringgold - Chattanooga in Union hands from late 1863) to May-Sep 1864 (the rest). Do not extend without evidence. headway_min 720 (about two trains a day each way) is an ESTIMATE, not sourced for this year range.

segments.note: Post-war State operation under governor-appointed superintendents, Atlanta Union Depot - Chattanooga Union Depot. The USMRR rebuilt and reopened the line through to Atlanta by 4 Jul 1865 and handed it back to the State on 25 Sep 1865 (not drawn: a military road, no civilian passenger train in hand). START is [OPEN]: 1867 is the first CONFIRMED post-war passenger year (Wikipedia cites an 1867 schedule with departures from Atlanta at 8:50 a.m. and 7 p.m.), NOT a known start - the bracket is 1865-1867 and no 1865-66 train is in hand; do not move the start earlier without evidence. End: the State leased the road to the Western & Atlantic Railroad Company from 27 Dec 1870 (ICC valuation); 1870 stays with the State. headway_min 720 reflects the two daily departures of the 1867 schedule; applying it to 1868-70 is an ESTIMATE.
sources: Segment-level: start from the 1867 schedule cited by Wikipedia; end from the ICC valuation abstract (lease date).

segments.note: Operated by the Western & Atlantic Railroad Company, the private lessee corporation headed by former governor Joseph E. Brown (23 investors, largely officers of connecting roads) - a different company from the State of Georgia, hence its own feature and colour (Rule 4). ICC valuation: 'December 27, 1870 to December 27, 1890: The Western & Atlantic Railroad Company operated the line under a lease approved October 24, 1870'. Year convention: 1871 (first full year) to 1890; 1870 is drawn for the State and 1891 onward for the NC&StL. 1889 Official Railway List: 55 locomotives, 41 passenger cars. Gauge changed 5 ft to standard 31 May - 1 Jun 1886 (not a split). headway_min 480 (about three trains a day each way) is an ESTIMATE, not sourced.
sources: Segment-level: dates from the ICC valuation abstract, railga.com and Wikipedia (lease of 27 Dec 1870, expiry 27 Dec 1890).

segments.note: The NC&StL's 'Dixie Line' south end, Atlanta - Chattanooga over the State's W&A, worked by the NC&StL as lessee from 27 Dec 1890 (ICC valuation: 'The entire property was leased to the carrier for 29 years under an act approved November 12, 1889'; lease renewed) to the NC&StL's merger into the L&N on 30 Aug 1957 (date as nashville_lines.geojson uses; railga 'merged into L&N in 1957'). The L&N's 1880 purchase of 55% of NC&StL stock did not change who ran the trains (not a split). 1890 is drawn for the W&A Railroad Company. Trains: Dixie Flyer (from 1892), Dixie Limited, Dixie Flagler (Chicago - Miami streamliner from Dec 1940, every third day), the Georgian (streamliner from 1946), plus locals. The Dec 1951 Official Guide (NC&StL Table 1) shows the Georgian at Chattanooga 6:25 AM / 4:00 PM and Atlanta Union Depot 9:55 AM / 7:45 PM, 'Dixie Flyer, Dixie Limited and The Georgian run daily', and indexes Acworth, Adairsville, Calhoun and Dalton as NC&StL stations. headway_min 360 is an ESTIMATE from that 1951 picture (three daily trains plus the tri-weekly Flagler and locals) applied across the whole span; earlier and later frequencies are not sourced.
sources: Segment-level: dates from the ICC valuation abstract and railga.com; 1951 trains from the Feb 1952 Official Guide (research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt, NC&StL Table 1 and the Index of Stations).

LATER ALIGNMENT (Rule 2): drawn on today's track throughout - the 1949-50 Lake Allatoona relocation (Acworth - Emerson), the Dec 1944 Etowah River bridge and the 1926-28 Chetoogeta tunnel. For 1957-1971 that is the correct era: all three relocations were complete by 1950. Atlanta: drawn to the 1930 Union Station site. (T5) Chattanooga: ends at the NC&StL junction (62 m join to the ncstl-nashville-chattanooga end vertex), ~1.1 mi short of the Union Station site; never on the parallel NS/CNO&TP track.

segments.note: The L&N ran the former NC&StL trains from the 30 Aug 1957 merger (the W&A lease passed with it). The Dixie Flagler/Dixieland and other NC&StL trains were dropped after 1957; the Dixie Flyer's Chicago - Atlanta service ended in Jan 1966 - CONFLICT recorded: one source has the final run an Atlanta - Chattanooga round trip on 20 Jan 1966, another the L&N section discontinued 12 Jan 1966 (same year either way). headway_min 480 is an ESTIMATE, not sourced.
sources: Segment-level: dates from Wikipedia (Dixie Flyer) and railfanning.org.

segments.note: The Georgian (Nos. 3/4 by 1970, Evansville - Atlanta) was the last passenger train: the Atlanta Union Station (1930) and Chattanooga Union Station articles both name it and end service on 30 Apr 1971, the eve of Amtrak (Amtrak never ran Atlanta - Chattanooga). CONFLICTS recorded: a Chattanooga Times retrospective gives the final departure from Chattanooga as 1 May 1971 and a forum rider a late southbound arrival on 2 May (trains in transit at midnight finishing their run) - 1971 either way; Wikipedia says the L&N dropped the name Georgian in 1968 (an unnamed Evansville - Atlanta train after), while railfanning.org calls the 1971 train the Georgian. Freight continued under the L&N, SCL, Family Lines and CSX (context only - not drawn, Rule 1). headway_min 1440 = one train each way a day.
sources: Segment-level: end date from Wikipedia (Union Station (Chattanooga); Atlanta Union Station (1930); Georgian) and railfanning.org.

No other straight-line leg. The alignment is the only one the branch had (no relocation known), so no later-alignment issue.

segments.note: Kingston (junction with the W&A) - Woolley's - Eves - Bass Ferry - Dykes - Freeman's - Second Avenue - Rome: the former Rome Railroad (opened c.1849, a separate company - not drawn here), bought by the NC&StL and run 'effectively as an extension of the Western & Atlantic'. START is the ownership year, NOT a timetable: the NC&StL acquired it 31 Dec 1896 (deed recorded 8 Jan 1897, evhsonline.org Kingston History); railga gives 1896 and one source 'circa 1894' - CONFLICT recorded, the deed date used. It is near-certain the NC&StL continued the Rome Railroad's passenger service (passengers were 'its main source of revenue'), but no 1897-1942 timetable was read. END: at the ICC abandonment hearing in Rome on 15 Jan 1943 a witness described the service in the present tense - 'It is a mixed train' (a mixed train counts as passenger service, Rule 1) - and the branch was abandoned later in 1943 (railga; one directory gives disposition 23 Oct 1943). 1943 is therefore the only DIRECTLY evidenced year; the 1897-1942 span rests on ownership plus continuity and is drawn as the report's drawable span, not as a [ANCHOR]. headway_min 1440 (one mixed train each way) is an ESTIMATE from the 1943 testimony, applied back without evidence.
